//: Every key is optional and every one has a default; a node starts with no file at all. Unknown keys are a hard error, so delete what you do not need rather than commenting it out. Precedence: defaults < this file < environment < flags.
//peers: Bare hosts (names or IPs). Every node uses the same gossip port, so no ports here; host:port is an escape hatch for one colliding entry. Including this node is fine — the self-join is skipped.
//advertise: The IP peers should dial. Set it on any host with more than one interface (WireGuard, Docker, a second NIC): autodetection picks the wrong one, and the symptom is a node that serves fine and sees only itself.
//frontend: Absolute URL at which this node's HTTP API is reachable, if it is not https://{advertise}:{http_port} — NAT, a load balancer, a name you would rather see printed. Decoration: nothing dials it.
//ssl: Relative paths resolve against the engine root, not against this file. Omit the block and drop certs at <root>/certs/server.{crt,key}, or set "insecure": true for local development.
//models: Empty loads every enabled descriptor under <root>/models. A non-empty list is an allow-list, and it gates the admin load route too — not only the startup preload.
//predict_timeout_ms: Ceiling on one request's execution budget. A smaller inbound grpc-timeout always wins; this only bounds callers that send none.
//max_inflight: Concurrently executing predictions. Defaults to this machine's CPU count clamped to 4..=16. It bounds both CPU oversubscription and coexisting response trees, so raise it deliberately.
//max_resident_models: Ceiling on resident models, dependency closures included.
//drain_delay_ms: How long to keep serving after a shutdown signal while /ready already answers 503, so load balancers and healthchecks observe the node leaving before its socket closes — and so the gossip departure reaches peers. 0 disables. A second signal skips it.
//warmup: Run one throwaway prediction per embedding model at boot, so /ready means 'answers at steady-state latency' rather than 'has finished loading'.
//manage: false keeps the registry's pull/activate/deactivate routes off the public port (the dashboard then cannot manage models). The loopback admin port always has them.
//web_ui: Directory of a built dashboard (index.html). Relative paths resolve against the engine root. Omit to serve <root>/server/ui, where the packages install it.
